The scenario's outcome variants, each classified success or failure; a route or recur from the scenario names one of them. :terminal is refused here: a scenario that ends the capability takes the terminal flag.

constructs.form: operation <operation-id> kind invoke-port port <port-id> | kind invoke-scenario scenario <scenario-id> | kind for-each port <port-id> over <path> [max <n>]
constructs.rule: invoke-port and for-each need a bind of the port in the same scenario; for-each folds the bound port over the collection at the path, at most max times (2147483647 without max). invoke-scenario names a scenario of this document; routes and invoke-scenario operations form no cycle.
The operation's outcome variants, each classified success or failure; :terminal marks a variant that ends the capability.
The declared-statement binding: the four keys platform, provider, statement and result attach to it and are all mandatory.

The platform-port binding: platform is mandatory, with provider, config or both. provider alone gives configuration {providerId}; config carries the port configuration verbatim, and a provider beside it is added as its providerId. statement and result are not admitted.

constructs.attachesTo: most recent bind or provider operation
constructs.rule: The port configuration verbatim: a single-line JSON object. "@provider-binding:<id>" strings resolve to the digest of the provider binding with that id; a name no provider binding declares refuses. Admitted on a platform bind, and after a provider operation, where it holds the static members of the provider's request.
Must name a platform capability declared in the estate.
Must name a provider declared in the estate.

Free text to end of line, trimmed.

Declares a sidecar provider-input-binding artifact: its JSON without the whitespace outside strings, addressed by sha256 over its UTF-8 bytes, compiled into the result providerBindings[]; configurations reference it as "@provider-binding:<id>". The author path mints the artifact as raw content-addressed authority in the same governed transaction.

One selection transition. Both scenarios and the variant on the from scenario are declared, and adjacent contracts agree. Routes form no cycle: a loop is a recur line. semanticProgress is terminating into a terminal scenario, otherwise narrowing.
At most one per capability, with a join over the same legs. Every leg runs concurrently (semanticProgress expanding); the capability's input and output contracts share one id.
At most one per capability; it converges the legs of the broadcast (the same set), all required. A join without a broadcast refuses. Settle and failure transitions are converging.

A bounded recurrence of one scenario on itself: both variants are declared on it, and its outcome contract equals its input contract. Without max the bound is 2147483647. semanticProgress is recurring.

The retained bytes of the canonical feature the source implements, read by that digest only, never through a binding (DSL_FEATURE_NOT_RETAINED when none). The source is checked against them as the no-drift check checks a declaration, and each finding refuses as DSL_FEATURE_DRIFT. One per source; the id is the capability's.

The operation hands its job to that capability of sidefx:capabilities, named exactly (DSL_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN otherwise). It compiles to <id>-vault, -credential, -open and -compose, which build the provider's request, and <id>, the generic capability invocation of the provider, whose result lands at result.

A member of the provider's request: from the scenario's request when the operation is the scenario's first, or from the result of the operation just before it (a provider's result is at result). Any other source refuses (DSL_VALUE_INVALID). The path is $ or $.<member>[.<member>...].

The scenario's outcome: that path of the result of the operation just before it. It compiles to <scenario>.outcome-vault, -credential and -open and <scenario>.outcome, whose statement selects the path. No operation may follow it in the scenario.

documentSemantics.mapping: capabilityId = the id
meaning.intent = the free text
meaning.outcome = the free text
inquiries[] += the free text, in order
cli.input = {type, contract: id}; contracts[] += {id, schema: the inline-json without the whitespace outside strings}
contracts[] += {id, schema}, once when its id is the input contract id
contracts[] += {id, schema: the inline-json}, after the input and output contracts
cli.display = {select, as}
cli.input.type = json or text; text adds cli.input.path = the payload path
cli.readings[] += {reading, altitudes[]}

scenarioId = id; name = id with - mapped to spaces, first letter capitalized; inputId = <id>-request; inputContract = input= or the input contract; eventId = <id>-requested; eventAuthority = <capabilityId>.v1 for the root, otherwise <id>.v1; outcomeId = <id>-outcome; outcomeContract = output= or the output contract; root and terminal
given = the free text
when = the free text
then = the free text
variants[] += {variantId, classification}

operations[] += {operationId, kind: invoke-port, portId} or {operationId, kind: invoke-scenario, scenarioId}; for-each: the bound port's configuration plus operationId, kind, portId, bodyCapabilityId = the platform, collectionValuePath, maximumIterations
outcomeVariants[] += {variantId, classification}, with terminal: true for :terminal
portBindings[] += {portId, platformCapabilityId: platform, configuration: {statement, resultColumn: result, providerId: provider}}
portBindings[] += {portId, platformCapabilityId: platform, configuration: the config verbatim with providerId = provider when both are given, or {providerId: provider}}

configuration = the inline-json verbatim, each "@provider-binding:<id>" replaced by that binding's sha256 digest; after a provider operation, the static members of the request its composing statement builds
providerBindings[] += {providerBindingId, digest, content}; "@provider-binding:<id>" inside any configuration resolves to the digest
routing[] += {transitionId: route-<from>-<variant>, fromScenario, variant, toScenario, topologyKind: selection, semanticProgress: terminating into a terminal scenario, otherwise narrowing}

routing[] += enter-<leg> {broadcast, groupId <capabilityId>.fan, semanticProgress expanding}; executionGraph = sda-semantic-execution-graph.v2 with dispatch authority <capabilityId>.dispatch and edge groups <capabilityId>.fan (all) and <capabilityId>.converge (all-required)
routing[] += settle-<leg> {join, groupId <capabilityId>.converge, joinSlotId <leg>, semanticProgress converging} and fail-<leg> {failure, the same group and slot, semanticProgress converging}

routing[] += recur-<scenario> {recurrence, variant: the continue variant, groupId <capabilityId>.recur-<scenario>, recurrenceAuthorityId, semanticProgress recurring}; executionGraph.recurrenceAuthorities[] += {continuationVariant, stopVariant, maximumIterations, authorityDigest}
feature = {capabilityId, digest: sha256:<hex>}; the result is REFUSED unless the source conforms to those bytes

operations[] += <id>-vault, -credential, -open, -compose and {operationId, kind: invoke-port, portId, providerCapabilityId, inputs}; portBindings[] += the vault, credential, open and statement ports and generic-capability-invocation.v1
inputs[] += {member, from, path}; the composing statement sets the member from the request, or from result for a provider just before
operations[] += <scenario>.outcome-vault, -credential, -open and <scenario>.outcome; its statement selects the path of the carrier
